domains.name: Apache Kafka
domains.description: Treating Apache Kafka like a traditional in-memory message queue—with random key distribution, small unbatched sends, or unbounded consumer processing delays—triggers partition ordering bugs, broker CPU saturation, and stop-the-world consumer group rebalance storms. Mastering Kafka requires thinking in immutable append-only commit logs, OS page-cache zero-copy (`sendfile`), ISR quorum durability (`acks=all` + `min.insync.replicas=2`), and cooperative incremental rebalancing.
topics: Why Sequential Disk + OS Page Cache Beats In-Memory Queues
ISR Replication, High Watermark & Idempotent Producer Sequence Numbers
Cooperative Incremental Rebalancing & Static Group Membership
Manual Offset Commits, Dead-Letter Topics & Hot-Partition Mitigation
Exactly-Once Semantics (EOS) Realities & When Not to Use Kafka

domains.name: Kubernetes
domains.description: Treating Kubernetes like a magic self-healing platform—while misconfiguring liveness probes, omitting `preStop` connection draining, setting `minAvailable: 100%` on PodDisruptionBudgets, or ignoring Linux CFS CPU throttling—causes rolling deployments to drop live traffic and freeze cluster upgrades. Production Kubernetes mastery means understanding the reconciliation loop (`API Server -> etcd -> Scheduler -> Kubelet`), decoupling readiness from liveness, right-sizing CPU/memory cgroups, and coordinating graceful pod termination.
topics: API Server, etcd Raft Quorum, Scheduler & Kubelet Watch Loops
Startup, Readiness & Liveness Probes + Zero-502 Termination Sequence
Linux CFS CPU Throttling, Memory OOMKill & The ndots:5 DNS Storm
PodDisruptionBudgets, Topology Spread & Automated Manifest Linter
StatefulSets, Storage Operators & When Managed Serverless Wins

domains.name: Large Language Models (LLM) Systems & Inference
domains.description: Serving Large Language Models in production fails when treated like stateless CPU microservices: autoregressive decoding is strictly GPU HBM memory-bandwidth bound, unpaged KV caches waste 60–80% of VRAM via fragmentation, and static request batching stalls fast users behind 2,000-token generations. Engineering high-throughput LLM gateways requires separating compute-bound Prefill from memory-bound Decode, paging KV-cache blocks (PagedAttention), caching shared system prefixes via radix trees, and enforcing deterministic schema + prompt-injection guardrails.
topics: Prefill vs. Decode, Arithmetic Intensity & KV-Cache VRAM Math
PagedAttention Block Tables & Radix-Tree Prefix Caching
Constrained FSM JSON Decoding & KV-Cache Capacity Calculator in Python
Prompt-Injection Sandboxing, Cascaded Model Routing & When Not to Use an LLM

domains.name: NoSQL Databases & Distributed Storage Engines
domains.description: Adopting Cassandra, DynamoDB, or MongoDB while modeling tables like normalized SQL schemas creates hot-partition throttling, tombstone read timeouts, and brittle application-side joins. Engineering high-scale NoSQL systems requires query-driven partition-key modeling, bounded time-bucketed partitions, LSM-Tree compaction discipline, and tunable quorum consistency (`R + W > N`).
topics: Query-Driven Modeling, Composite Keys & Time-Bucketed Partitions
MemTables, SSTables, Bloom Filters & Compaction Strategies
Tunable Quorums (R + W > N), Read Repair & Tombstone Storms
Quorum Overlap Verifier & Tombstone-Safe Write Builder in Python
Secondary Index Traps, Cross-Partition Transactions & When SQL Wins
